2.text: below.” — “How wonderful! What for?” — “Now listen! A man of my

3.text: people is sick. He suffers greatly. Therefore I come to you for help.” —

4.text: “Ho! It is wonderful! And what says the other woman?” — “She says, ‘Go

5.text: and see what the chief inhabitant will say!’” — “Indeed! Wait a moment

6.text: till I come out. It cannot be that you have travelled such a long distance

7.text: without any result.” Then I gather a weed from the top of that hummock,

8.text: as if it were the old woman whom I am taking with me. We come back

9.text: to the first house. “Halloo!” Now there are two of us. My companion

10.text: cries out, “O mother! let us go! It must not be that this man has come

11.text: hither without any good result.” — “Ay, ay! Wait for me! I am coming!”

12.text: Now I gather another blade of grass, and I carry both of them to the house,

13.text: as if I had returned from a land very far off, from beyond the sky. All the

14.text: people of the house are waiting for me. I put the two old women beside

15.text: the suffering man, close to his pillow. In the morning we prepare two tiny

16.text: bags with little pieces of skin. Small bits of fat are put into them, and shreds

17.text: of sinew into each bag separately. This represents the payment to the old

18.text: women in meat and thongs. Then I take them back to their former place,

19.text: and I leave each of them at their respective hummock house. After that I

20.text: come back, pretending again to return from beyond the sky.¹

21.text: (b) When I am sick, I demand assistance from the Right Side of the

22.text: Morning-Dawn. “Oh, help my need; look down upon me with the Godly

23.text: Substance (añaˊñ-vaˊɪrg̣ɪn)!” The Right Side of the Morning-Dawn answers,

24.text: “I refuse!” — “O you, the Top of the Dawn, help my need; look down upon

25.text: me with the Godly Substance!” The Top of the Dawn answers, “I refuse!”

26.text: From the Left Side of the Morning-Dawn I ask for assistance. “Help my

27.text: need; look down upon me with the Godly Substance!” The Left Side of the

28.text: Morning-Dawn answers, “I refuse!” I ask the Front Head (the star Arcturus),

29.text: “Help my need; look down upon me with the Godly Substance!” The Front

30.text: Head answers, “Ask the Rear Head (the star Vega). Near the right corner

31.text: of thy house there abides a Woman of Light, a Hummock-Woman, an Old

32.text: Woman from the Time of the First Creation: ask her for an incantation!”

33.text: I visit her. “What have you come for?” — “I am suffering! Look down

34.text: upon me with the Godly Substance!” — “Well, I will try!” She gives me a

35.text: blade of grass, an iron blade, which is an iron hawk. I rub my body with

36.text: that grass, and draw out the disease, which I turn into a flock of ptarmigan.

37.text: These are to be caught and eaten by the iron hawk.²

38.text: (a) and (b) told by a Reindeer Chukchee of the Kolyma Country.

39.text: (c) When a man is suffering, they call the Man from the Upper Region,

40.text: and they speak thus: “Come down! I want to use you for my ‘assistant.’
